dedupe_keys.name: gpsjam daily maps of likely gnss interference from aircraft ads b reports

description: GPSJam, created by John Wiseman in July 2022, maps where aircraft report degraded navigation accuracy, a strong sign of GPS or other satellite navigation jamming. Many aircraft broadcast ADS-B messages that include the accuracy of their navigation system; GPSJam aggregates these reports from the community receiver network airplanes.live and from ADS-B Exchange over 24 hours into hexagons, counting aircraft with good and bad accuracy, and colours hexagons where more than 2 or 10 percent of aircraft report low accuracy. Coverage: worldwide where ADS-B receivers exist, daily from 14 February 2022, with conflict zones such as the Baltic, the Middle East and Ukraine prominent. Format and access: an interactive map and daily gzip-compressed CSV files at gpsjam.org/data (H3 hexagon id, counts of good and bad aircraft) with a manifest of dates, free to use. Caveats: low accuracy can have causes other than jamming, the navigation system is not identified, coverage depends on receivers and air traffic, and the author flags suspect days. Simulation uses: a record of security threats to satellite positioning for hazard exposure of GNSS-dependent services such as aviation, shipping, telecom timing and power grids. Related records: IGS products and the FAA WAAS reports give GNSS performance, and ENISA incident reports cover telecom incidents.
